title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
authors: François Gay-Balmaz, Tudor S. Ratiu, Cesare Tronci
abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
summary: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework to model the coupled, conservative dynamics between topological defects (vortices/disclinations) and the background fields in systems like quantum fluids and liquid crystals. By merging the Euler-Poincaré approach with gauge theory, the authors derive coupled equations that govern the interaction, providing key insights into conserved quantities like helicity.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a unified, conservative dynamical model that accurately describes the coupled evolution between topological defects (like vortices and disclinations) and the background fields in condensed matter systems.
main_result: The authors propose a framework combining the Euler-Poincaré variational setting with gauge theory, yielding a coupled system that predicts specific conserved quantities, such as hydrodynamic helicity, for ideal dynamics.
method: The methodology involves combining advanced mathematical tools—specifically the Euler-Poincaré formalism and gauge theory—to derive coupled equations of motion for both the field variables and the defect structures.
model_or_system: The study applies to two primary physical systems: quantum fluids (modeled via the Gross-Pitaevskii theory exhibiting vortices) and nematic liquid crystals (modeled using the Ericksen-Leslie framework exhibiting disclinations).
key_observables: Vortex line evolution, disclination density, quantum vorticity, Madelung flow, and the angular momentum component along the director field.
important_parameters: The model is restricted to ideal, reversible (conservative) dynamics, and the analysis often involves regularization techniques to handle singular defect filaments.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes ideal, non-dissipative dynamics and explicitly excludes the physics of defect reconnection or the inclusion of full inertial/dissipative effects.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure suggests derivations of coupled equations (e.g., Biot-Savart-Schrödinger system, hydrodynamic equations) and the identification of conserved invariants.
paper_structure: The paper is structured to first address quantum vortices ($\S 2$), then disclination dynamics in nematic textures ($\S 3$), and finally generalizing the framework to flowing nematic liquid crystals ($\S 4$).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding how topological defects fundamentally alter the dynamics of quantum fields, bridging concepts from fluid dynamics, gauge theory, and quantum many-body physics.
